verdict_rationale: No P0 (deception) or P1 (correctness) blocking issues found. The recipe has a real SHA256, genuine R34 API tests calling Moose class definition/attributes/inheritance/type-constraints/metaclass, proper R32 platform checks, no R33 hardcoded compiler env vars, honest status marking (built=not published), and no binary artifacts. P2 style warnings and P3 hints are documented below for improvement.

check_1_R34_real_api_test.detail: test_moose.sh defines Animal/Dog Moose classes with 'has' attributes, 'extends' inheritance, type constraints (isa => 'Str'), metaclass introspection (->meta->get_all_attributes). Not a print-only stub.

check_2_conanfile_platform_hardcoded.detail: R32: uses 'self.settings.os not in ("Linux", "OHOS")'. R33: no ${CC}/${CFLAGS} hardcoding. LD is unset (os.environ.pop) not set to a hardcoded compiler. install_base uses os.path.join(self.build_folder, ...) not hardcoded paths.

check_3_sha256_real.detail: conandata.yml sha256='c4bdcbe4daaeb50dcf40ea17dfb1483db22cb8832287abd8762a44ab98fb561f' — 64 hex chars, not all-zero/ff, not REPLACE_WITH_ACTUAL_SHA256.

check_4_manifest_real_tests.detail: MANIFEST.yml lists 3 real upstream tests (t/000_load.t, t/basics/basic_class_setup.t 29 tests, t/attributes/attribute_delegation.t 107 tests) with commands. No TODO placeholders.

check_5_no_deception.detail: No fake status (built=honest, not published). No empty stub tests. test_moose.sh exits 1 for real errors. Permission denied tolerance is clearly logged as [warn] with platform limitation explanation.

check_6_patch_validity.detail: conandata.yml references 3 patch files (0001-Makefile.PL.patch, 0002-lib-Class-MOP.pm.patch, 0003-lib-Class-MOP-PurePerl.pm.patch) but these files are NOT in the changed_files list. Cannot verify diff format validity. If patches are new for this version, they must be committed to the repo; if already present from a prior commit, no action needed.

check_7_test_moose_validation_sequence.detail: test_moose.sh Step 1 verifies .so ELF validity (file + grep ELF), Step 2 verifies .pm version string (grep 2.4000), Step 2b verifies PurePerl patch in Class/MOP.pm (grep PurePerl), THEN Step 3 attempts API test. Prior no-op P1 is addressed.

check_8_package_type_library_shared.detail: conanfile.py: package_type = "library", options = {"shared": [True, False]}, default_options = {"shared": False}.

check_9_patch_descriptions_concise.detail: Descriptions: 'Bypass compiler check for OHOS', 'Pure Perl fallback for XS load', 'PP implementations of XS methods' — all concise, space-separated.

check_10_manifest_build_system_custom.detail: Software-level manifest.yaml has build_system: custom. Version-level manifest.yaml has build_system: perl_makefile (top-level) but build.system: custom (under build:). The software-level manifest satisfies check #10.

issues.description: Shell script does not start with 'set -euo pipefail'. Rule #7 requires all shell scripts to begin with safe mode: set -e (exit on error), set -u (undefined variable error), set -o pipefail (pipe failure propagation).
issues.evidence: Script starts with shebang and comments, then jumps directly to PERL_LIB="$1" without any set directives.
issues.suggestion: Add 'set -eu' after the shebang line. Note: 'pipefail' requires bash/zsh; if using #!/bin/sh, at minimum add 'set -eu'. Consider switching to #!/bin/bash to support full 'set -euo pipefail'.

issues.description: conandata.yml declares 3 patch files (patches/0001-Makefile.PL.patch, patches/0002-lib-Class-MOP.pm.patch, patches/0003-lib-Class-MOP-PurePerl.pm.patch) but none appear in the changed_files list or file_contents. Cannot verify that patches are valid diff format or that they exist in the repository. For a new recipe version where conanfile.py (109 lines, all additions) and conandata.yml (17 lines, all additions) are new, the patches should also be new and included in the PR.
issues.evidence: changed_files list contains 8 entries; no patches/*.patch files. diff_stat shows no patches/ directory entries. conanfile.py export_sources() calls export_conandata_patches(self) which requires patch files to physically exist.
issues.suggestion: Verify patches/ directory exists in the repository with all 3 .patch files. If patches were committed in a prior commit, no action needed. If patches are missing, the build will fail at apply_conandata_patches(self).

issues.description: Version-level manifest.yaml top-level build_system is 'perl_makefile', which is not in the standard allowed list (cmake | autotools | makefile | meson). The software-level manifest correctly uses 'custom'. The version-level manifest also has build.system: custom under the build: key, creating inconsistency between top-level build_system and build.system.
issues.evidence: Top-level: build_system: perl_makefile. Under build:: system: custom. Software-level manifest: build_system: custom.
issues.suggestion: Change version-level top-level build_system to 'custom' for consistency with the software-level manifest and the build.system field. Or use 'makefile' if the standard list should be followed.

issues.rule: code_style.13 (conandata.yml URL must be HTTPS) + review_memory.II.13 (R39 official source)
issues.description: Version-level manifest.yaml source.url uses 'http://www.cpan.org/...' instead of HTTPS. CPAN supports HTTPS. The conandata.yml correctly uses 'https://cpan.metacpan.org/...'. While manifest.yaml source.url is metadata (not the actual Conan download URL), the code style rule prohibits http:// URLs.
issues.suggestion: Change to https://www.cpan.org/... or align with conandata.yml's https://cpan.metacpan.org/... URL.

issues.description: Version-level manifest.yaml source.sha256 is empty string (""). While the actual SHA256 is correctly provided in conandata.yml (c4bdcbe...561f), the manifest.yaml metadata has an empty sha256 field. This is not deception (the real hash exists in conandata.yml) but is a metadata completeness issue that could cause confusion.
issues.suggestion: Populate manifest.yaml source.sha256 with the same value as conandata.yml: c4bdcbe4daaeb50dcf40ea17dfb1483db22cb8832287abd8762a44ab98fb561f

issues.rule: code_style.10 (shell error handling — no || true without comment)
issues.description: Line 'OUTPUT=$(perl -I"$PERL_ARCH_DIR" -MMoose -e '1' 2>&1 || true)' uses || true to prevent command failure from exiting the script. While the purpose is clear from context (capturing error output for platform-limitation detection), there is no inline comment explaining why the error is intentionally ignored, as required by rule #10.
issues.suggestion: Add inline comment: 'OUTPUT=$(perl -I"$PERL_ARCH_DIR" -MMoose -e '1' 2>&1 || true)  # capture load error output for platform-limitation check'

issues.description: Script uses '#!/bin/sh' instead of '#!/usr/bin/zsh' as shown in the code style example. While #!/bin/sh is more portable and standard, the rule example specifically shows #!/usr/bin/zsh. Using /bin/sh also prevents use of 'set -o pipefail' which requires bash/zsh.
issues.suggestion: Consider using '#!/bin/bash' or '#!/usr/bin/zsh' to enable full 'set -euo pipefail' support, or keep #!/bin/sh with 'set -eu' only.

issues.description: Some [ok]/[fail] lines lack the 8-space indent specified by rule #9, while later lines (e.g., line 139: '        [ok] Package integrity verified...') do have it. The format is inconsistent — early [ok]/[fail] lines are at column 0, later ones have 8-space indent.
issues.evidence: Line 22: echo "[ok] Found Moose.so: $SO_FILE" (no indent) vs Line 139: echo "        [ok] Package integrity verified..." (8-space indent).
issues.suggestion: Apply consistent 8-space indent to all [ok]/[fail] sub-item lines under [step] markers for visual alignment.

issues.description: package_info() does not set self.cpp_info.libs. Rule #4 states 'package_info() must set cpp_info.libs'. However, the inline comment explains 'No cpp_info.libs — this is not a linkable C library'. This is a Perl XS module where .so is loaded by Perl's XSLoader at runtime, not linked by C/C++ compilers. The rule is designed for C/C++ libraries and may not apply to Perl XS modules.
issues.suggestion: This is an acceptable exception for Perl XS modules. Consider adding a rule clarification for non-C-linkable library types. The runenv_info.append_path('PERL5LIB', d) correctly exposes the Perl module path to consumers.

issues.rule: review_memory.I.1 (R34 — test must call API, not just verify files)
issues.description: The test tolerates 'Can\'t locate ... .pm' errors by exiting 0 after verifying package integrity. While the rationale (missing Perl runtime dependency = system env, not build defect) is documented in comments, this means the actual Moose API test may not execute if Perl dependencies are missing in the test environment. The script does verify .so ELF validity, .pm version string, and PurePerl patch before this tolerance, so package integrity is confirmed. However, a consumer test that never calls the API provides weaker assurance.
issues.suggestion: Consider requiring at minimum a 'perl -e "use Moose; print Moose->VERSION"' smoke test that doesn't require complex dependencies, or document in the test that the full API test is conditional on Perl dependency availability.

issues.description: Version-level manifest.yaml build.configure_options contains 'INSTALL_BASE=/storage/Users/currentUser/usr/local' — a hardcoded absolute path. This is in metadata/documentation only; the conanfile.py correctly uses os.path.join(self.build_folder, 'lib', 'perl5') which is dynamic. The metadata path documents the original build environment but could be confusing.
issues.suggestion: Consider replacing the hardcoded path in metadata with a generic placeholder like 'INSTALL_BASE=<build_folder>/lib/perl5' or noting it was the original build machine path.

issues.description: conanfile.py does not define a layout() method. Rule #3 lists the standard method order as: export_sources → requirements → layout → source → generate → build → package → package_info. The layout() method is optional in Conan 2.x (defaults are used), but its absence means the standard order is technically incomplete.
issues.suggestion: If no custom layout is needed, this is acceptable. Consider adding a comment or empty layout() if strict method-order compliance is desired.

summary: The perl-moose 2.4000 Conan recipe passes the audit with no P0 (deception) or P1 (correctness) blocking issues. The recipe demonstrates genuine adaptation work for HarmonyOS: Makefile.PL compiler-check bypass for HMDFS dlopen restriction, Pure Perl fallback for Class::MOP when XS .so cannot load, and LD environment variable management. The test_package properly calls real Moose API (R34 satisfied) — defining classes with attributes, inheritance, type constraints, and metaclass introspection. The test_moose.sh correctly validates .so ELF validity, .pm version string, and PurePerl patch presence before attempting the API test (check #7 satisfied). SHA256 is real (check #3). MANIFEST.yml lists real upstream tests (check #4). conanfile.py has package_type=library with shared option (check #8). Software-level manifest has build_system=custom (check #10). Six P2 style warnings include: missing set -euo pipefail in test_moose.sh, patch files not verifiable in changed_files, version-level manifest inconsistencies (build_system value, http:// URL, empty sha256), and || true without comment. Six P3 hints include shebang choice, output format inconsistency, cpp_info.libs exception for Perl XS, test tolerance leniency, hardcoded path in metadata, and missing layout method. Overall verdict: APPROVE with warnings — the recipe is functionally correct and honest, with style improvements recommended.
